video_title: Fabolous On Why Early 2000s Hip-Hop Was Different & How Social Media Changed Rap

quotes.speaker: Vince Carter
quotes.summary_phrase: Vince Carter on the unique playing styles of his era
quotes.excerpt: I didn't play like Vince. Vince didn't play like Paul Pierce. We all had our unique styles.

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Carter
text_blocks.text: I didn't play like Vince. Vince didn't play like Paul Pierce. We all had our unique styles because of how we grew up and how we consumed the game of basketball.

text_blocks.speaker: Fabolous
text_blocks.text: That's the same way I looked at it at the time. When I look back, I'm like, damn, like you just said, it was this one, it was that one, and everybody had their own base, their own foundation.

quotes.speaker: Fabolous
quotes.summary_phrase: Fabolous on the loss of originality in modern hip-hop
quotes.excerpt: Everybody is trying to sound like the other person or whoever has a hit.
quotes.quote: I think that's even one of the criticisms that they say about hip-hop now is that it blended a little bit where everybody is trying to sound like the other person or whoever has a hit, people try to sound like that.

quotes.speaker: Vince Carter
quotes.summary_phrase: Vince Carter on Michael Jordan's unparalleled versatility in the 80s
quotes.excerpt: That 85 to 90 Mike was we never seen him. That Mike, the versatility, the speed.

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Carter
text_blocks.text: That 85 to 90 Mike was we never seen him. That Mike, the versatility, the speed, everything that he did, I think his first five years, more of the mid 90s to where Mike was playing in the triangle, mid post, that's what Phil Jackson era. I'm talking about Phil Jackson, that's what Kobe Bryant, right, that's who he copied, that guy.

text_blocks.speaker: Tracy McGrady
text_blocks.text: So you're talking about Phil Jackson era.

quotes.speaker: Vince Carter
quotes.summary_phrase: Vince Carter on how the triangle offense elevated Michael Jordan
quotes.excerpt: I think he came up with that suited Mike to be in the triangle.

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Carter
text_blocks.text: I think he came up with that suited Mike to be in the triangle because of double team, so much attention that you receive. So now putting you in that triangle, you could see all angles of where defenses are coming from the double team. And for me, I think having that system is what, Mike is going to be Mike, but I think in terms of winning and taking him to another level, that triangle definitely put him there.

text_blocks.speaker: Tracy McGrady
text_blocks.text: So when I'm saying near, do you think Phil brought that to Kobe? Like, yo, you should do some of these stuff Mike was doing because it works in this triangle offense.

quotes.speaker: Fabolous
quotes.summary_phrase: Fabolous on how singles defined his artistic image
quotes.excerpt: Singles for me were like selling me as the artist that you wanted to buy into.
quotes.quote: Singles for me were like selling me as the artist that you wanted to buy into. I would make songs, especially in that time. I think hip-hop has evolved where you don't really have to do that in a sense, but in that time you had to make a record that spoke to what your image was going to be in hip-hop.
